# P3.5 Native audio in WebKitGTK, with a spoken English fixture

| Field | Value |

## Objective
WebKitGTK **captures** microphone audio inside the Linux app window and hands
it to the note's own transcript path, proven with intelligible synthetic English
speech; and silence or a tone never produces a note.

This card is **capture-only** (owner decision 2026-10-02, `AM-109`). It proves
two things and defers everything else to **S4a.2**:

- **Proved here:** the real `getUserMedia` → `AudioContext` → `AudioWorkletNode`
  → WAV path (`web/src/lib/recorder.ts`) receives frames from the host's capture
  device; the app's own record button really starts and stops it; the finished
  WAV is really POSTed by the app to `/api/transcribe`; and neither a tone nor
  digital silence creates a note.
- **Deferred to S4a.2 (the transcription half):** every claim about *words* —
  that the transcript contains the negated risk statement and the dose, the
  `transcription_empty` assertion, whisper accuracy, model selection (A07) and
  the `whisper_model` setting. **No model is acquired, downloaded, selected or
  run by this card** (HS-3; A07 belongs to S4a.2, which is `NOT STARTED`). A row
  that would need a model to pass is written here as deferred to S4a.2, never as
  a row that fails.

## Fixed decisions

### The fixture
- Piper (A09) with **`en_US-ljspeech-medium`** (A10) — the voice
  `docs/research/es-mx-speech.md` §5.3 recommends, public-domain training data,
  22,050 Hz. Text: a fabricated 30-second progress dictation about **John
  Smith** with one negated risk statement ("no self-harm thoughts this month")
  and one dose ("continue the sertraline fifty milligrams daily") — HS-8, the
  prototype's sample person, and no other name.
- **Generated at test time into the sandbox run folder and never committed.**
  §5.4 is explicit that no voice's model card states a position on
  redistributing generated audio, so L-POLICY row 4 forbids committing it. The
  raw 22,050 Hz Piper output is deleted in the same row; only the 16 kHz
  artefact survives, and it lives under `<sandbox>`.

### The one test-only hook (`web/src/main.tsx`)
There is no driver for a WebKitGTK window: Playwright drives Chromium only
(`e2e/fixtures/audio/README.md:5-7`), and P3.3's harness runs "no stub, no fake
bridge line and no test hook" (`scripts/v2/tauri-lifecycle.test.mjs:12-14`).
Owner decision `AM-109` permits **exactly one** such hook in `web/`. It is:

- **File:** `web/src/main.tsx`, the entry point every build loads, beside the
  boot-time side effects it already owns (`applyTheme`, `installAutoHideScrollbars`).
  Not `Capture.tsx`, not `useLiveRecording.ts`: the harness has to reach the
  capture screen from the home screen, and a hook mounted only on the capture
  screen cannot report the two clicks before it. **No other `web/` file changes**,
  so no component, no prop, no route, no type and no test outside `main.tsx`
  moves.
- **Gate:** Vite's built-in env prefix, with **no config change**:
  `import.meta.env.VITE_APUNTA_TEST_IDENTITY === '1'`. Vite replaces every
  `import.meta.env.VITE_*` reference at build time and defaults an absent one to
  `undefined` (`node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:25363`,
  `define["import.meta.env.*"] = "undefined"`; the default prefix is `VITE_`,
  same file `:5931`). The hook is one `if` around one block: absent variable →
  `undefined === '1'` → dead branch, removed by the bundler's minifier.
  `web/vite.config.ts` declares no `envPrefix`, no `define` and no test env, so
  nothing else can switch it on.
- **Release-build evidence (the gate cannot exist in a release build):**
  1. The only producer of a shipped bundle is
     `scripts/v2/package-linux-resources.sh:104`, which runs
     `npm run build` and copies `web/dist`
     (`:155-160`); `npm run build` reaches the web workspace's `vite build`
     (`web/package.json`). None of `package.json`, `package-linux-resources.sh`,
     `scripts/package-mac.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` or any other script in
     this repository sets `VITE_APUNTA_TEST_IDENTITY` — a repository-wide search
     finds no occurrence outside this card and `vite.config.ts`'s absence of it.
     The only `VITE_` string in shipped code is the unrelated
     `VITE_HOST = '127.0.0.1:5173'` constant in
     `server/src/http/request-guard.ts:32`.
  2. The **only** build that sets it is this card's V2 row, which prefixes the
     flag inline on the `npm run build` it runs before `npm run tauri:build:test`
     (`tauri:build:test` = `tauri build --features test-identity --config
     src-tauri/tauri.test.conf.json`, P3.3's gate). A release build
     (`npm run tauri:build`, `npm run package:mac`) never carries it.
  3. V2 asserts the positive half mechanically: after the flagged build, the
     hook's marker string **is** present in `web/dist/assets/*.js`; V5's
     invariant, restated for any later release build, is that a release
     `web/dist` must contain **zero** occurrences. A release build that ever
     contains the marker is a `FAIL` and an owner escalation, not a row to be
     relaxed.
- **What the hook does — nothing but report.** It publishes, and it never
  actuates:
  - the **screen rectangle** of named elements, so the harness can put a real
    pointer click on the real button: `[data-testid='home-action-note']`,
    `[data-testid='home-search']`, the first `li[role='option']` in the home
    results list, `[data-testid='record-start']`, `[data-testid='record-stop']`
    (`HomeLauncher.tsx:136,166`, `Capture.tsx:360,426` — attributes that already
    exist for e2e, added by nothing here);
  - the **capture state** it reads out of the DOM the app already renders:
    which of `record-start` / `record-stop` / `record-stage` / `record-done` /
    `capture-error` is present (the phase, `Capture.tsx:344-435`), the
    `record-timer` text (`LiveRecording.tsx:66-68`) and the `--level` custom
    property on `record-dot` (`LiveRecording.tsx:60-65`).
  - **The trigger is a real click.** The harness clicks those rectangles with
    `xdotool mousemove --sync --window <id> <x> <y> click 1`; the app's own
    `onClick` handlers run (`HomeLauncher.start` → `navigate('/capture/<id>')`,
    `Capture.startRecording` → `useLiveRecording.start`, `Capture.stopRecording`
    → `process()` → `POST /api/transcribe`). Nothing in `web/`, `server/` or
    `src-tauri/` is asked for a new capability, a new IPC command, a new route
    or a new Rust API — there is none.
  - **Delivery channel, and why it is one that works headlessly:** the marker
    line is written to `document.title` **and** with `console.info`, and — the
    channel the harness *requires* — as a same-origin
    `fetch('/p3.5-marker?...')`, whose URL Fastify's request logger
    (`server/src/app.ts:69`, logger on by default) writes to its own stdout. The
    AppImage's shell and the bundled server inherit the AppImage's stdout, the
    harness already captures that pipe (`tauri-lifecycle.test.mjs:214-247`) and
    already prints it as evidence (`:764-774`), so the marker arrives on a pipe
    this repository has been reading for three cards. The same origin means no
    new network access (HS-6: loopback only, the server Apunta already talks
    to); the marker carries **phase, timer and level only** — never a patient
    name, never transcript text, never anything from the live instance. The
    other two channels are conveniences and the harness records which of the
    three delivered the line.
  - It polls on a 250 ms interval and re-publishes only on change, so the
    harness always has a current rectangle; it removes its interval and its
    listeners when the flag is off, which is every release build.
- **Privacy of the marker:** HS-8 holds — the only name in the run is John
  Smith, created by the harness through the API in the sandbox run folder, never
  read from the live instance.

### Microphone containment (the host-global mutation)
The host's default capture device is a **real USB microphone**
(`alsa_input.usb-UGREEN_Camera_2K_…`). The run must never touch it. Owner
decision `AM-109`:

- **The virtual PipeWire source is the ONE permitted host-global mutation
  outside the run folder.** Nothing else in this card changes host state: the
  data folder, the port, the cache/config/XDG homes and the display all come
  from the sandbox environment and the harness, as in P3.3.
- **Mechanism, pinned for this host: PipeWire through `pactl` only.** This host
  runs `pipewire-pulse`; there is no `pulseaudio` daemon and no `pacmd`, and
  **neither may be used or installed**. The modules are provided by
  pipewire-pulse's own Pulse module layer — `module-null-sink` and
  `module-remap-source` are both implemented in
  `/usr/lib/pipewire-0.3/libpipewire-module-protocol-pulse.so` (verified by
  `strings`, read-only; no module was loaded while this card was written).
  `pactl` is 17.0 (`pactl --version`), so `pactl get-default-source` exists.
- **Exact commands, in this order, from the repo root:**

  ```sh
  PREV_DEFAULT="$(pactl get-default-source)"                     # 1. remember
  SINK_ID="$(pactl load-module module-null-sink \
      sink_name=apunta_p35 sink_properties=device.description=Apunta_P3.5)"
  SRC_ID="$(pactl load-module module-remap-source \
      source_name=apunta_p35_mic master=apunta_p35.monitor)"    # 2. create
  pactl set-default-source appointa_p35_mic                     # 3. default
  paplay --device=apunta_p35 --rate=16000 --channels=1 \
      "$(dirname "$APUNTA_DATA_DIR")/audio-en/dictation-30s.wav" &   # 4. feed
  #   ... the harness launches the AppImage and drives the real buttons ...
  pactl set-default-source "$PREV_DEFAULT"                      # 5. restore
  pactl unload-module "$SRC_ID"; pactl unload-module "$SINK_ID"  # 6. remove
  ```

  The names are `apunta_p35` / `apunta_p35_mic` in every row, so two runs never
  collide and V5 can assert on them exactly.
- **Step 3 happens before the AppImage is launched, and step 4 before the record
  click.** The default is what WebKitGTK's `getUserMedia` opens, so the real
  microphone is not merely un-defaulted, it is not the device the app asks for.
- **`trap`-based removal, on every exit path.** The harness installs
  `process.on('SIGINT'|'SIGTERM'|'SIGHUP')` and an exit handler that runs
  `pactl set-default-source "$PREV_DEFAULT"` and both `unload-module` calls, in
  that order, whether the row passed, failed, threw or was signalled. A row that
  cannot restore and remove is a `FAIL`, not a cleanup detail: the owner's
  microphone must be the default again whatever happened.
- **The playing stream is stopped by pid** (C-ISO@1 rule 7: never `pkill`), and
  `paplay` is never pointed at a sink other than `apunta_p35`, so the owner's
  audio output is untouched.
- **V5 is the only check that the source is gone** — and it is checked from the
  outside, not from the harness's own bookkeeping.

### The relationship with the Spanish generator (no second wrapper)
`scripts/v2/generate-es-audio.mjs` already solves most of V1: it takes
`PIPER_BIN` and `PIPER_MODEL` as environment inputs, refuses an output path
inside this repository and refuses a path directly under `/tmp/apunta-v2`
(`:263-286`), pins the synthesis (`--noise_scale 0 --noise_w 0`,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`), resamples Piper's 22,050 Hz to 16 kHz mono 16-bit with
`ffmpeg` and `bitexact` flags (`:624-653`), and writes a `reference.json` of
provenance; `check-es-audio.mjs` is its checker. **P3.5 uses exactly those
inputs, exactly that resample rule and exactly that refusal**, and V1 is the
literal command that does it — which is why:

- **`scripts/v2/make-en-audio.sh` is dropped from May edit.** A second bash
  wrapper around Piper is the exact defect the review named (D6): it could
  write audio into the repository, undoing the refusal the Spanish script
  exists to enforce, and it would be a weaker copy of a working tool.
- **Why a separate script is nevertheless not required:** V1 needs **one**
  30-second clip and **one** 10-second silence clip — not a 295-clip corpus, no
  seeded variants, no SNR arm and no `reference.json`. A row that runs Piper
  once and resamples once is shorter than the refusal logic any new script would
  need, and it is reviewable in the card.
- **The refusal is enforced twice anyway, in code the harness owns:**
  `scripts/v2/tauri-audio.test.mjs` refuses any `--audio` directory that is
  inside this repository or sits directly under `/tmp/apunta-v2`, exactly as
  `generate-es-audio.mjs:276-281` does, and V1's output path is *derived* from
  `$APUNTA_DATA_DIR` (`$(dirname "$APUNTA_DATA_DIR")/audio-en`), so it cannot be
  anywhere else.
- If a later card wants one English corpus rather than one clip, extending the
  two `.mjs` scripts is the right move and needs an amendment; this card does not
  assume it.

- **Wrapper mode: `env`**, exactly as P3.3 does, because these rows launch the
  native AppImage window and the app starts its own server. The harness requires

  them (`tauri-lifecycle.test.mjs:69-84`); every row therefore sources the
  printed `export` lines. The AppImage is resolved once by the harness, with zero
  or more than one match a failure (`resolveAppImage`, same file `:88-97`), and
  is the path **V2 built**: `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage`.
- **Pinned Node, in every row:** `export
  PATH="$HOME/.local/share/apunta-node/node-v24.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH" && node
  --version` printing exactly `v24.19.0`. The box default is outside
  `engines: ">=24.19.0 <25"` and `sandbox.mjs` spawns with `process.execPath`.
- **Piper is not on `PATH` and must not be installed.** The venv is at
  `~/.local/share/apunta-piper/venv` (`piper` at `venv/bin/piper`, piper-tts
  1.8.0 — `docs/v2/evidence/S4a.1/acquisitions.md`), so V1 and V3/V4 pass

  branch is **not** applicable: it is installed.
- **Microphone access is granted only when the requesting origin is the app's
  own `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`** — the sandbox port this run was assigned, and
  no other. Any other origin is refused, and the refusal is asserted, not merely
  implemented.
- **GStreamer plugins (A03) only if a failing test shows they are missing**; the
  `apt` command goes to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md` and the card stops
  there. Agents never enter a password.
- **Row ids.** The old V2/V3/V4 (spoken capture, tone+silence, source removed)
  are now **V3, V4 and V5**; **V0** (host) and **V2** (the flagged test build)
  are new, and V2 must pass before V3 and V4 can mean anything. No assertion,
  threshold or expected result from the previous text was removed or weakened;
  V3's and V4's `transcription_empty` clause became an explicit S4a.2 deferral,

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-ISO@1 Isolation and the sandbox wrapper

**Built by** P0.3. **Proven by** P0.3 (negative tests) and Q1.1.
**Consumers:** every card that starts a server, opens a real database, runs
e2e, runs `check:format`/`check:refine`, runs a real-model eval or launches
the app.

**Interface** (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs`, Node, no dependencies):

| Command | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs run --port <p> -- <cmd...>` | Creates run folder, starts server, verifies ownership, runs `<cmd>` with the sandbox environment, stops only what it started, exits with `<cmd>`'s code |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port <p>` | Creates run folder only, prints `export` lines for tools that start their own server (Playwright) |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs selftest` | Runs the negative cases below; exit 0 only if all refuse correctly |

**Rules**
1. Run folder: `/tmp/apunta-v2/<runId>/` with `data/`, `logs/`, `tmp/`,
   mode `700`. `runId` = UTC timestamp + 8 random hex characters.
   `realpath` of every path must stay under `/tmp/apunta-v2/`; a symlink that
   escapes is refused.
2. Port must be an integer 7800 to 7889 and free (checked by binding, then
   released immediately before the server binds). 7717 is always refused.
   7890 to 7899 are reserved for the updater test server (C-UPD) and refused
   here.
3. The data folder is never the platform default. The wrapper computes the
   default with `platformDataDir()` (C-PATH) **as a string only** and refuses
   if the sandbox path equals it or is inside it. It never lists or opens the
   default.
4. Server environment: `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, `APUNTA_PORT`, `APUNTA_NO_OPEN=1`,
   `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID=<runId>`, `APUNTA_V2=1`. When `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID` is
   set, `/api/health` includes `"testRunId"`; the field never appears
   otherwise.
5. Ownership check: the wrapper polls `/api/health` for up to 30 s and
   proceeds only if `testRunId` equals its `runId`. Anything else (no
   answer, a different id, no id) is refused and the child is stopped.
6. Child command environment adds `APUNTA_CHECK_URL`, `APUNTA_E2E_PORT`,
   `APUNTA_V2=1`.
7. Cleanup kills only the process group the wrapper created. Never `pkill`,
   never the Ollama daemon.
8. When `APUNTA_V2=1`: Playwright sets `reuseExistingServer: false`;
   `scripts/check-note-format.mjs` and `scripts/check-refine.mjs` exit 2 if
   `APUNTA_CHECK_URL` is unset or points at port 7717.

**Normal example.** `sandbox.mjs run --port 7801 -- npm run check:format`
→ run folder created, server answers with the matching `testRunId`, the
check runs against `http://127.0.0.1:7801`, server stopped, exit code of the
check.

**Rejection examples** (each must be a `selftest` case, refused before any
database is opened): `--port 7717`; `--port 7890`; port in use by a dummy
listener; a dummy server on the port answering `/api/health` with 200 but no
or wrong `testRunId`; run folder symlinked outside `/tmp/apunta-v2/`;
`APUNTA_DATA_DIR` equal to the platform default string.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

| A15 | `prism-ml/Bonsai-4B-gguf`, the single file `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf` and nothing else in the repository | `huggingface.co` (prism-ml/Bonsai-4B-gguf) | Hugging Face CDN hosts, on A07's terms | A07's | no | none (measurement only) |
| A16 | `Fraunces[SOFT,WONK,opsz,wght].ttf` from `github.com/google/fonts` at `ofl/fraunces`, SHA-256 `177ff6c0f14e5550a3c624247cd1189611d4eb65d000b14944c63d967958abbb`, plus its OFL 1.1 text. **Committed to the repo** beside Kalam's, used only to generate the wordmark and A outlines | `github.com` (one fetch, then never again) | `raw.githubusercontent.com` | none | no — outlines only, no font file in the bundle | P2.1 (owner amendment 2026-09-27) |

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
